label: Maserati 4.7 L V8 (Quattroporte S, F136 YG, cross-plane)
based_on: Maserati F136 YG 4.7 L V8, Quattroporte S, 2008-2010

sources.what: Maserati Quattroporte owner's manual, US edition, M139 (book dated 1 September 2008, 2009 model year), hosted by the Maserati Club UK (a ManualsLib download). Manufacturer document: technical specifications p. 226 for the 4.2 (M139 A) and 4.7 (M139 R) versions.

Maserati Academy, 'Maserati Range Technical Updates', July 2012, training documentation for the Maserati service network (cited by Wikipedia's F136 article). Read from the Wayback Machine copy http://web.archive.org/web/20220327103955/https://academy.maserati.com/wbt/upload/lmsIveco-1564/011704-Product_Update_Course_EN.pdf because the original host refused connections; manufacturer document.
Wikipedia, Ferrari F136 engine: variant table (engine codes, years, power, torque, sump type) sourced to the Maserati Academy, and the cross-plane statement.
Autozine (Mark Wan), Quattroporte V review: Quattroporte S 430 hp at 7000 rpm, 361 lbft at 4750 rpm.

Wikipedia, Maserati Quattroporte: fifth-generation engine paragraph (cross-plane crank, intake-side continuous variable valve timing, F136S dry sump in DuoSelect cars); quad round tailpipes on the standard cars; Sport GT S bypass-valve exhaust.

notes: Sourced from Maserati's 2009 Quattroporte owner's manual: bore and stroke 94 x 84.5 mm, 4691 cc, compression 11.02:1, 90-degree V8, four valves per cylinder, firing order 1-8-6-2-7-3-4-5, wet sump, 317 kW (EC; 425 HP in the US manual, 430 elsewhere) at 7000 rpm and 490 N m at 4750 rpm. From the Maserati Academy (2012 service training): engine code F136 YG for the Quattroporte S, intake-only variable timing with 60 crank degrees of range, the cam-setting values, and 7600 rpm as the highest engine speed (used as redline; reading it as the limiter is ours). Cross-plane crank and intake-only variable timing: Wikipedia (F136 and Quattroporte articles). The firing order 1-8-6-2-7-3-4-5 is Maserati's; the numbering (1-4 one bank, 5-8 the other, 1 and 5 sharing the front pin) is our inference, the only common numbering under which that order is a cross-plane order. The cam is entered at 0.6 mm valve lift. Exhaust closing at 0.6 mm is at TDC, from the Maserati Academy's workshop cam-setting values (F136 YG). Those values put the intake at 0.6 mm lift 25 degrees after TDC with the phaser at rest; with 60 crank degrees of intake phasing the intake can open at 0.6 mm anywhere from 25 degrees after TDC to 35 degrees before TDC. The model has one fixed cam: the intake is entered opening 15 degrees before TDC at 0.6 mm (an estimate inside that range), so the phaser's effect on the torque curve is not represented. Estimated, not sourced: connecting-rod length (140 mm), valve diameters, cam lift (10.5 mm intake, 9.5 mm exhaust), cam durations, the fixed intake-cam position, intake runner length and diameter, exhaust primary length and diameter, the exhaust layout after the heads (entered as 4-into-1 per bank, each bank its own pipe to the rear with no crossover), pipe diameters, idle speed (750 rpm). Left to the simulator's defaults: plenum, throttle and airbox, collector volume, mufflers, flywheel inertia. Also estimates: friction_scale 0.9, heat_q 2.6e6 and burn_scale 0.92 (inside their allowed ranges, none at a limit), set with the cam, runner and primary figures so that simulated torque and power come near the published figures; no sourced number was changed. The Quattroporte S has the standard exhaust; the bypass-valve silencers belong to the Sport GT S (Academy) and are not modelled. Not modelled: the intake phaser, any variable intake geometry (none found either way), catalytic converters as separate elements.
